A terminal in my pocket: Blink, Tailscale and a computer that never sleeps

The problem it solves

Most of my data-science work does not fit into a laptop session. Scrapers run for days, model fits take hours, and a pipeline should not die because I closed a lid or left the house. On top of that I work on several computers, and I want to check on a job from the sofa, the train or a conference hall, not only from my desk.

The general idea

Four small pieces that fit together:

  • A computer at home that is always on runs the long jobs. It does not care about batteries, lids or Wi-Fi hotels.
  • Tailscale puts all my devices on one private network, with a stable name for each. No port forwarding, nothing exposed to the internet.
  • The terminal is the one interface that is identical on a laptop, a Linux box and a phone, and it is tiny in bandwidth.
  • tmux keeps every job in a session that survives disconnects, so I can detach, leave and attach again later.

Examples

Starting a long scrape on the home computer and leaving it running:

ssh home-pc
tmux new -s scrape
uv run python scrape.py      # detach with Ctrl-b d

Checking on it from anywhere, for example from my phone:

ssh home-pc
tmux attach -t scrape

On the phone I use Blink Shell, a proper terminal for iOS with SSH and Mosh. Mosh is what makes it pleasant on mobile: the connection survives switching between Wi-Fi and mobile data and the phone going to sleep.

Tips from my setup

  • Tailscale on every device, the phone included. My network has a Mac Studio, a MacBook, two Linux computers, an iPad and an iPhone, and ssh machine-name works between all of them.
  • A physical keyboard for the phone. I use a Clicks keyboard case. Typing code on glass is the weak spot, and with real keys, fixing a path or restarting a job from the sofa becomes comfortable.
  • One place for everything. Work on every machine lives in tmux, and herdr, the terminal workspace manager I use next to it, shows my workspaces and their state in one sidebar, so I see which session is busy and which agent is waiting for me.
  • Move files without thinking. A small just recipe asks which device I mean, lets me pick the file with a fuzzy finder and runs scp. See the post about just.
  • Make the home computer boring. Sleep disabled, a wired connection and nothing else running on it.
